attribution.note: Marcus's own closing line in his own Substack post. The quoted NYT material around it is context, not the claim.

semantics.note: The line is sarcastic, but it states as fact that a system unfit for taxes is being used for lethal operations by parts of Washington. The proposition keeps his scope and wording and adds no firmer reliability claim.

contract.note: Reading 'blow people up' as targeting support for strikes, not autonomous weapon release, is the ordinary informed reading. Treating the tax premise as 'unreliable without verification' is fair. Ending the period at publication suits a year-to-date observation.

evidence.note: Guardian report (first published Mar 1, available before the cutoff) citing WSJ and Axios: the US military used Claude to help select targets in the Iran strikes that began Feb 28. Sourcing is secondhand but identified.
A contemporaneous Mar 5 reproduction of the NYT test: four chatbots, Claude among them, got refunds wrong by over $2,000 on average, even when given all forms. This supports the tax premise.
Anthropic's own disclosure. It confirms military deployment and says fully autonomous weapons were excluded. That rules out autonomous use but does not contradict human-directed targeting support.

Later syndicated copy of the NYT article: Claude got one refund right but made many errors elsewhere, and experts urge keeping humans involved. This qualifies the premise without showing dependable unverified filing.

reviews.rationale: Reputable reporting (e1) shows US military command used Claude, a generative model, to help select targets in strikes on Iran from Feb 28, inside the target period. NYT testing (e2, with context in e4) shows chatbots made material errors preparing returns. e3 and e4 only qualify the claim and contradict neither part. Both parts of the plain reading are met.
